les: Water word geleen, nie gemaak nie
kaps_punt: Die siklus van waterverbruik: hoe water van die natuurlike siklus onttrek en gebruik word en weer na see terugvloei

items.bewering: Jy ken reeds die natuurlike watersiklus en sy vier stappe.
items.blok: Mense haal water uit die siklus
items.bron: Common teaching model of four stages (evaporation, condensation, precipitation, collection): Westfield State University teacher-education page (westfield.ma.edu .../watercycle/question2.html); National Geographic Kids water-cycle page; Hydro Tasmania lesson plan (hydro.com.au). Note: the hydrological science (Wikipedia 'Water cycle', USGS Water Science School) names more processes than four, so 'vier stappe' is true as the school model and not as a complete scientific count. Acceptable at Grade 4; noted so it is not mistaken for an exhaustive claim.

items.bewering: Die reën uit daardie siklus vul riviere en opgaardamme met varswater.
items.blok: Mense haal water uit die siklus
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Water cycle' (precipitation, surface runoff into rivers and lakes); DWS/GCIS Water and Sanitation yearbook chapter (surface water stored in dams).

items.bewering: In baie dorpe en stede haal mense die water uit 'n opgaardam en stuur dit na 'n watersuiweringsentrum.
items.blok: Mense haal water uit die siklus
items.bron: Rand Water (Engineering News 2023; Wikipedia 'Rand Water'): Vaal Dam water treated at Zuikerbosch and Vereeniging purification works; City of Cape Town Water and Sanitation: 14 dams, 12 water treatment works. The qualifier 'baie' is right: groundwater supplies about 350 SA towns and villages (DWS National State of Water Report 2024 - Groundwater; Beaufort West ~90% boreholes).

items.bewering: Daar word dit skoongemaak en daarna in 'n reservoir gestoor.
items.blok: Mense haal water uit die siklus
items.bron: Rand Water via Engineering News (2023-03-03): purified water pumped from the purification works to pump stations and on to 59 storage reservoirs, from which municipalities distribute; City of Cape Town: 180 reservoirs.

items.bewering: Groot pype dra die skoon water na huise, skole, hospitale, fabrieke en ander geboue.
items.blok: Mense haal water uit die siklus
items.bron: Rand Water: 3 600 km of large-bore pipes delivering bulk water to municipalities, mines and industrial users (Daily Maverick 2025-02-13; Engineering News); City of Cape Town reticulation 'distributes drinking water to consumers ... through a network of pipelines, pump stations and reservoirs'.

items.bewering: Mense drink die water en kook daarmee by die huis. Hulle bad ook daarin en was hul klere daarmee.
items.bron: Domestic use as described by City of Cape Town Water and Sanitation and the DWS/GCIS yearbook (municipal/domestic use ~27% of national use). Everyday uses, no contrary source.

items.bewering: Boere lei hul gewasse nat en gee hul diere water.
items.bron: DWS (NWRS-2 via Deputy Minister speech to Agri SA, 2019; GCIS yearbook 2022/23): agriculture is the largest user at about 60-61%, irrigation the largest single use, livestock listed separately. The sentence is true; how it sits in the lesson's route is raised under 'Waar die twee siklusse inhaak'.

items.bewering: Fabrieke gebruik water om produkte te maak en masjiene af te koel.
items.bron: Eskom 'CO 0005 Cooling Techniques' and Eskom water re-use fact sheet (eskom.co.za): water used for cooling, with evaporation ~80% of a wet-cooled station's requirement; DWS/GCIS yearbook lists bulk industrial use as a water-use sector.

items.bewering: Die gebruikte water verdwyn nie, maar ná 'n bad of die wasgoed is dit vol seep en vuil.
items.bron: USGS Water Science School, 'Die Hidrologiese Siklus' (Afrikaans): water you drink is not new, 'dit was nog altyd hier en is deel van die natuurlike watersiklus'; Wikipedia 'Water cycle': the mass of water on Earth remains fairly constant. Greywater from bathing and laundry carries soap and dirt (City of Cape Town greywater guidance). True at the level of the whole cycle; the lesson's own 'skaars en kosbaar' close stops it reading as 'water is never lost to us'.

items.bewering: In dorpe en stede loop baie van die gebruikte water deur rioolpype na 'n rioolwatersuiweringsaanleg.
items.bron: City of Cape Town reticulation 'conveys wastewater to treatment works through a network of pipelines'; eThekwini: 27 sites where sewage is treated before discharge to a river or the ocean (Daily News/The Mercury 2023-12-20). 'Baie' is right: not all used water reaches a works (Cape Town marine outfalls, GroundUp; homes without sewers).

items.bewering: Daar word die water skoongemaak en dan terug na riviere en ander waterbronne gestuur.
items.bron: DWS-linked description (search result on DWS wastewater): 'Waste Water Treatment Works remove waste from the water and then return the water to the rivers', effluent required to meet DWS standards; eThekwini discharges treated effluent to rivers or the ocean. True as what a works does; that many works fail is raised under 'Geleen, nie gemaak nie'.

items.bewering: Die riviere dra hierdie water verder. Onderweg verdamp 'n deel van die water en 'n deel trek in die grond in.
items.blok: Van die rivier na die see
items.bron: DWS National Water Resource Strategy (2004), Appendix D14 Lower Orange: large evaporation and transmission losses along the river; Wikipedia 'Water cycle' (infiltration, evaporation from surface water).

items.bewering: Tog vloei baie van die water uiteindelik weer terug na die see.
items.blok: Van die rivier na die see
items.bron: DWS NWRS Appendix D14 Lower Orange and ORASECOM study (ais.unwater.org): roughly 5 500 million m3 a year still reaches the Orange mouth, about half the natural flow. 'Baie' (not 'al') is the correct quantifier; it does not claim all water reaches the sea.

items.bewering: Dit is dieselfde invloei wat jy reeds uit die watersiklus ken.
items.blok: Van die rivier na die see
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Water cycle' and the four-stage teaching model (collection/runoff into rivers and the sea): river flow to the sea is part of the natural cycle. Substance confirmed. Note only: I found no Afrikaans hydrology source using 'invloei' as the name of that stage (USGS Afrikaans page gives no stage terms); the word literally means inflow, so it is a terminology choice for the series, not a factual error.

items.bewering: By die see tel die natuurlike watersiklus die water weer op, en onderweg ook al by die riviere en die grond. Die son laat dit verdamp, wolke vorm en reën val.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Water cycle': solar radiation is the main energy source for evaporation; 86% of global evaporation is over the ocean, the rest from land, soil and surface water; vapour condenses into clouds and precipitates.

items.bewering: Die reën vul weer die riviere en opgaardamme waar mense se pad met die water begin het.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Water cycle'; Rand Water / City of Cape Town (dams fed by rainfall runoff).

items.bewering: So haak die twee siklusse op twee plekke in mekaar. By die opgaardam haal mense water uit die natuurlike siklus en by die rivier of die see gaan dit weer terug.
items.bron: Intake: groundwater supplies about 350 SA towns and villages, Beaufort West ~90% from boreholes (DWS National State of Water Report 2024 - Groundwater; Kouga Express/novanews); raw water is also abstracted straight from rivers (gov.za DWS statement on drinking-water quality). Return: irrigation, about 60% of all SA water use (DWS NWRS-2), returns only 40-60% as return flow and the rest leaves the field as evaporation and plant transpiration (USGS chapter 11H; US National Weather Service consumptive-use papers); wet cooling towers lose about 80% of their water to evaporation (Eskom CO 0005 Cooling Techniques); some water soaks into the ground. Cape Town's marine outfalls send sewage straight to the sea (GroundUp) - that one fits 'die see'.
items.regstelling: Tested as a set with blocks 1-4, the two-hook model is exact only for the town route the lesson follows (dam -> purification -> pipes -> sewer -> works -> river/sea), and block 1 itself qualifies that route with 'In baie dorpe en stede'. But this sentence states it for 'die twee siklusse' in general, and the begrip defines the siklus van waterverbruik generally - so a learner will conclude water is only ever taken at a dam and only ever comes back at a river or the sea. False for the biggest user the lesson names: a farmer's irrigation water (block 2) mostly goes back into the air from the field, not down a river; and many towns take water from boreholes or straight from rivers. Narrow the quantifier to the route described rather than cutting the idea, e.g. say that on the path this lesson followed the two cycles hook together at the dam and at the river or sea. If words allow, one clause that some used water goes straight back into the air (from irrigated fields) closes the gap; do not add groundwater detail the lesson does not otherwise need. Also check block 2: placed directly after the piped clean water, 'Mense gebruik die water ... Boere lei hul gewasse nat' reads as if farms irrigate with purified tap water; most irrigation water is untreated water from rivers, dams and canals. Every sentence there is true; the adjacency builds the false picture.

items.bewering: Mense se pad met water is dus 'n lus uit die natuurlike siklus en weer terug daarin. Dit is nie 'n pad wat iewers ophou nie.
items.bron: USGS 'Die Hidrologiese Siklus' (Afrikaans): drinking water 'was nog altyd hier en is deel van die natuurlike watersiklus'; Wikipedia 'Water cycle': Earth's water mass fairly constant. Used water rejoins the cycle by some route (river, sea, air, ground), so 'loop' and 'does not stop somewhere' hold at whole-cycle level. Holds only because it does not name where it rejoins; the two-place restriction is the separate item above.

items.bewering: Ons noem hierdie hele lus die siklus van waterverbruik.
items.bron: Stipulative name, identical to the CAPS bullet the lesson records in kaps_punt ('Die siklus van waterverbruik: ...'). I located the DBE KABV Sosiale Wetenskappe Gr 4-6 Afrikaans PDF (education.gov.za) but my fetch truncated after its two cover pages, so the wording was not independently read there; naming risk is negligible because the lesson defines the term itself.

items.bewering: Mense maak nie self water nie, maar leen dit by die natuurlike siklus. (also the title: 'Water word geleen, nie gemaak nie')
items.bron: USGS 'Die Hidrologiese Siklus' (Afrikaans): water is not new, it was always here as part of the natural cycle; Wikipedia 'Water cycle' (mass constant). Mapping checked: borrowing = taking something that stays the lender's, using it, giving it back. Holds: water is taken from and returned to the cycle. The usual place a borrowing image breaks (you return it as you got it) is pre-empted by the next sentence, which says it comes back dirtier and must be cleaned. Desalination does not break it: it takes seawater from the same cycle and makes no new water.

items.bewering: Ná gebruik is baie van die geleende water vuiler as toe hulle dit gekry het.
items.bron: Green Drop 2022 (DWS, reported by GroundUp and Daily Maverick): municipal wastewater requires treatment before discharge; DWS effluent standards. 'Baie' correctly avoids 'all'.

items.bewering: Daarom moet dit skoongemaak word voordat dit kan teruggaan. ... Elke keer kos daardie skoonmaak tyd, geld en energie.
items.bron: DWS Green Drop Report 2022 (GroundUp 'Half of South Africa's sewage treatment works are failing'; Daily Maverick 2022-04-07 and 2022-06-21): 334 of 850 municipal works in a critical state; billions of litres of raw or partially treated sewage enter rivers and the sea every year (e.g. Emfuleni into the Vaal). GroundUp: Cape Town's Green Point, Camps Bay and Hout Bay outfalls discharge essentially raw sewage to the sea, screened only.
items.regstelling: 'Moet ... voordat dit KAN teruggaan', followed by 'Elke keer kos daardie skoonmaak', reads as a description: dirty water cannot get back into the cycle unless it is cleaned, and it is cleaned every time. That is the 'all used water is cleaned and returned' picture, and in South Africa it is false - dirty water does get back, uncleaned, and that is exactly what pollutes rivers. Make it plainly a should, with the reason: the water must be cleaned before it can go back SAFELY (otherwise it dirties the rivers and the sea). Keep the cost sentence; once the previous sentence is a 'should', 'Elke keer' reads as 'every time it is cleaned', which is true (wastewater works are big electricity users - GreenCape Factsheet 5: water and wastewater ~17% of municipal energy, aeration up to 75% of a works' energy).

items.bewering: Water uit 'n opgaardam moet ook skoongemaak word voordat mense dit drink.
items.bron: gov.za DWS statement on drinking-water quality during the cholera outbreak: raw water abstracted from rivers and dams is treated by water boards or municipalities before supply to households; Rand Water purification of Vaal Dam water.

items.bewering: Elke keer kos daardie skoonmaak tyd, geld en energie.
items.bron: GreenCape Factsheet 5 'Energy Efficiency in Secondary Treatment Technologies': water supply and wastewater treatment ~17% of SA municipal energy, wastewater up to 25% of some municipalities' electricity bills, aeration up to 75% of a works' energy; Green Drop 2022: R8.1 billion needed to restore works. The cost claim itself is true; the 'Elke keer' reading it inherits is raised in the item above.

items.bewering: Dat water nie verdwyn nie, beteken dus nie dat ons dit kan mors nie. Skoon varswater bly skaars en kosbaar.
items.bron: gov.za 'Government on water scarcity and drought' (13 Nov 2015) and GCIS Water and Sanitation yearbook: South Africa is the 30th driest country, ~500 mm average rainfall against a world average of ~860 mm; weet.co.za/USGS: only about 3.5% of Earth's water is fresh, most of it frozen.

items.bewering: siklus van waterverbruik: Hoe mense water uit die natuurlike siklus haal, dit gebruik en dit teruggee.
items.bron: Read alone: matches the CAPS bullet recorded in the lesson (onttrek, gebruik, terugvloei) and is true at whole-cycle level per USGS 'Die Hidrologiese Siklus'. It names no single return point and claims no cleaning, so it carries neither fault raised above.

opsomming: Twee dinge moet reg: die les se 'op twee plekke' (water uit by die dam, terug by die rivier of see) word as die hele siklus van waterverbruik gestel, maar boere se besproeiingswater, die grootste gebruik in SA, gaan grotendeels as damp terug en baie dorpe gebruik boorgate; en 'moet skoongemaak word voordat dit kan teruggaan ... elke keer' leer dat gebruikte water altyd skoongemaak word, terwyl die 2022 Green Drop-verslag rou riool in riviere en die see aanteken - albei is met 'n smaller kwantor of 'veilig' reg te maak; geen oortreffende trappe in die les nie, en die 'geleen'-vergelyking hou.
